extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, third-party administrators, pharmacy benefit managers, plan sponsors, and legal counsel/stakeholders subject to Section 1557
extracted.subtask_short: section 1557 applicability for issuers and TPAs
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule guidance on when and how Section 1557 applies to health insurance issuers, excepted benefits (including Medigap and STLDI), third-party administrators, and pharmacy benefit managers, and how OCR allocates liability and conducts fact-specific investigations of discriminatory benefit design features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to all operations of a principally engaged recipient issuer, including excepted benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule applies to all operations of a recipient health insurance issuer when principally engaged, including an issuer's excepted benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR interprets section 1557's phrase “any health program or activity, any part of which is receiving Federal financial assistance” to cover an issuer's other plans and products as part of the issuer's operations when the issuer is principally engaged in providing/administrating health insurance coverage. See preamble citations (e.g., 87 FR 47844-45; 87 FR 47875-76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case, fact-specific investigative approach
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR's analysis for investigating a potentially discriminatory benefit design is necessarily a fact-specific, case-by-case analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR evaluates the nature, scope, and contours of the specific plan at issue and an alleged discriminatory design feature in light of the entity's stated coverage parameters. This approach applies across plans, including major medical coverage and excepted benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered entities may articulate legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities have the opportunity to articulate a legitimate, nondiscriminatory basis for their challenged action or practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigating, OCR will evaluate such justifications and consider context (including Federal or State law requirements) in assessing whether a challenged design feature violates section 1557; OCR will work with covered entities to achieve compliance and avoid market disruptions where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medigap coverage when issuer is principally engaged
rubrics_metrics.description: Medigap plans, though an excepted benefit, are subject to the rule if offered by a recipient issuer that is principally engaged in the provision or administration of health insurance coverage or other health-related coverage as specified under § 92.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR acknowledges Medigap's standardized, Federal/State-regulated nature (including open enrollment and underwriting constraints) and will take State/Federal law requirements into account when evaluating potentially discriminatory features. Nonetheless, section 1557 would preempt any State law requiring conduct prohibited by section 1557 as applied to a recipient issuer.

rubrics_metrics.name: STLDI coverage when issuer is principally engaged
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term limited duration insurance (STLDI) plans would be covered under the rule as part of a recipient issuer's operations if the issuer is principally engaged as set forth in § 92.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes STLDI's statutory exclusions from other ACA requirements but concludes that exclusion from the PHS Act definition of individual health insurance does not exclude such coverage from section 1557; OCR notes risks these plans pose to protected groups and reasons for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party administrators (TPAs) covered when part of operations or recipients/subrecipients
rubrics_metrics.description: An issuer's or other entity's operations related to third party administrative services are subject to the rule when the issuer receives Federal financial assistance and is principally engaged, and a third party administrator could be covered if it is a recipient or subrecipient of Federal financial assistance or part of a principally engaged recipient's operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will engage in a fact-specific analysis to evaluate whether a third party administrator is appropriately covered under section 1557 in circumstances where the TPA is legally separate from the issuer that receives Federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability follows the entity responsible for the challenged decision or action
rubrics_metrics.description: When investigating complaints relating to third party administrators that are covered, OCR will determine whether responsibility for the decision or alleged discriminatory action lies with the plan sponsor or the covered TPA, and will process the complaint against the entity responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the alleged discrimination relates to administration by a covered TPA, OCR will proceed against the TPA. If the discriminatory benefit design originated with the plan sponsor/plan, OCR may refer the complaint to EEOC or DOJ; OCR will refer FEHB/FEDVIP/FLTCIP matters to OPM.

rubrics_metrics.name: TPA not liable for plan design when it exercised no control or role in development
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR does not intend to enforce the rule against a third party administrator for a plan design that it did not design and over which it has no control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will consider which party was responsible for the alleged discriminatory conduct; where the discriminatory terms originated with the plan sponsor or plan and the TPA played no role in development, OCR will refer to other agencies as appropriate rather than pursue the TPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: TPA can be liable when it developed discriminatory plan designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered third party administrator could be liable for a discriminatory design feature when the discriminatory terms originated with the third party administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the plan sponsor subsequently adopted the plan, case law supports liability for TPAs that design and offer standard plan designs containing discriminatory features; OCR will pursue such claims against the TPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERISA does not exempt entities from complying with section 1557
rubrics_metrics.description: ERISA's requirement that plans be administered according to plan terms does not invalidate or impair section 1557 obligations, and ERISA is not to be construed to impair or supersede other Federal laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR's approach recognizes ERISA duties but relies on precedent holding that ERISA does not shield entities from complying with nondiscrimination obligations under other Federal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered entity remains liable when outsourcing design/implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity that outsources the implementation or benefit design of discriminatory plans remains liable under this rule for any discriminatory plan terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outsourcing to an entity not covered by section 1557 does not absolve the covered recipient of responsibility for discriminatory plan terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) treated similarly to TPAs when covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharmacy benefit managers are health programs or activities and would be covered under the rule if they receive Federal financial assistance or are part of the operations of a principally engaged recipient; their liability under the rule would be similar to that of covered TPAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OCR receives a complaint about a covered PBM, OCR will evaluate whether the PBM or the plan sponsor is responsible for the challenged action using the same analysis applied to TPAs (designing formularies, utilization management, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purely administrative actions alone are not discriminatory acts if merely relaying plan terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative actions such as developing documents or preparing policy booklets for clients, alone, would not constitute third party administrator liability for discriminatory plan design features to the extent the covered TPA is merely relaying information consistent with underlying plan terms that it played no role in developing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR affirms that mere relay of plan terms does not by itself violate the rule, distinguishing administrative implementation from design or decision-making that produces discriminatory effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR will consider State/Federal law requirements as context but will preempt conflicting state law
rubrics_metrics.description: When investigating a discriminatory design feature, OCR will evaluate the covered entity's legitimate nondiscriminatory reason; if the reason is based on a Federal or State law requirement, OCR will take this into account in evaluating the context of the challenged design feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR also states that section 1557 would preempt a State law Medigap requirement—or any other excepted benefit requirement—that compelled conduct prohibited by section 1557 as applied to a recipient health insurance issuer subject to section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR may refer or transfer matters to other Federal agencies when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of OCR's enforcement authority, OCR has the option of referring or transferring matters to other Federal agencies with jurisdiction over the entity (e.g., EEOC, DOJ, OPM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will transfer matters where it lacks jurisdiction over an employer responsible for benefit design of employer-sponsored group health plan coverage, and will refer FEHB/FEDVIP/FLTCIP complaints to OPM.
